title: Your robot teacher of the future
paragraphs: Will your job be done by a robot in the future? Bank of England economists predict that almost half of all UK jobs are under threat of automation. Those most at risk involve repetitive manual labour, such as factory positions. But could even the venerable profession of teaching soon have to compete against powerful electronic educators?

At first glance, teaching might seem impervious to replacement by robots. Teachers use a range of soft skills that machines find hard to replicate. They gauge pupils‘ needs and tailor feedback accordingly. They adapt materials to make them more engaging and effective. And they provide pastoral care: looking out for students who lag behind or disrupt the class.

Nonetheless, some believe the future of education will be technological. In an interview with Business Insider magazine, futurist Thomas Frey predicts that “by 2030 the largest company on the internet is going to be an education-based company that we haven’t heard of yet.”

He thinks that ’bots’ - online robot teachers - will make education so efficient that students will be able to compress an entire undergraduate degree into six months of learning. A bot learns what your “idiosyncrasies” “interests” and “reference points” are, “and it figures out how to teach you in a faster and faster way over time,” according to Frey.

Whether or not such incredible speeds will be reached, over the last decade there has been a huge increase in online learning platforms. Companies such as Udemy and Khan Academy produce courses that allow millions to learn at home for free, at their own pace. But there are limitations. Without the face-to-face stimulation of a classroom environment, the overwhelming majority of students fail to complete online courses. How to sustain motivation to learn is one more skill that online teachers will need to master.

Indeed, Frey admits there is some way to go: “Nobody has quite cracked the code for the future of education.” What do teachers themselves think about this? Professor Donald Clark from Derby University in the UK thinks that we should embrace change, even though people will lose their jobs.
“Artificial intelligence will destroy jobs - so why not use it for a social good such as learning?” he asked.

vocabulary.entry: under threat of [phr.] /ˈʌndə θret əv/ 在……的威胁下
vocabulary.example: Many species are under threat of extinction.
vocabulary.translation: 许多物种面临灭绝的威胁。

vocabulary.entry: automation [n.] /ˌɔːtəˈmeɪʃən/ 自动化
vocabulary.example: Automation has replaced many factory jobs.
vocabulary.translation: 自动化已经取代了许多工厂工作。

vocabulary.entry: repetitive [adj.] /rɪˈpetətɪv/ 重复的；反复的
vocabulary.example: The job was boring and repetitive.
vocabulary.translation: 这份工作枯燥且重复。

vocabulary.entry: manual labour [n.] /ˌmænjuəl ˈleɪbə/ 体力劳动
vocabulary.example: Manual labour is physically demanding.
vocabulary.translation: 体力劳动对身体要求很高。

vocabulary.entry: venerable [adj.] /ˈvenərəbəl/ 值得尊敬的；历史悠久的
vocabulary.example: The venerable professor has taught for forty years.
vocabulary.translation: 这位德高望重的教授已经执教四十年。

vocabulary.entry: at first glance [phr.] /ət fɜːst ɡlɑːns/ 乍一看
vocabulary.example: At first glance, the problem seems easy.
vocabulary.translation: 乍一看，这个问题似乎很简单。

vocabulary.entry: impervious to [adj.] /ɪmˈpɜːviəs tuː/ 不受……影响的 (正式用语)
vocabulary.example: He is impervious to criticism.
vocabulary.translation: 他对批评无动于衷。

vocabulary.entry: replicate [v.] /ˈreplɪkeɪt/ 复制；重复
vocabulary.example: It is difficult to replicate the success of the original.
vocabulary.translation: 很难复制原版的成功。

vocabulary.entry: gauge [v.] /ɡeɪdʒ/ 评估；判断
vocabulary.example: Teachers gauge students‘ understanding through tests.
vocabulary.translation: 教师通过测试评估学生的理解程度。

vocabulary.entry: tailor [v.] /ˈteɪlə/ 调整；使适应
vocabulary.example: The course is tailored to individual needs.
vocabulary.translation: 这门课程是根据个人需求调整的。

vocabulary.entry: pastoral care [n.] /ˌpɑːstərəl ˈkeə/ 精神关怀；教牧关怀
vocabulary.example: The school provides excellent pastoral care for students.
vocabulary.translation: 这所学校为学生提供出色的精神关怀。

vocabulary.entry: lag behind [phr.] /læɡ bɪˈhaɪnd/ 落后；滞后
vocabulary.example: If you don't study, you will lag behind others.
vocabulary.translation: 如果你不学习，就会落后于别人。

vocabulary.entry: disrupt [v.] /dɪsˈrʌpt/ 扰乱；使中断
vocabulary.example: The protest disrupted traffic in the city.
vocabulary.translation: 抗议活动扰乱了城市的交通。

vocabulary.entry: nonetheless [adv.] /ˌnʌnðəˈles/ 尽管如此；然而
vocabulary.example: The weather was bad; nonetheless, we went out.
vocabulary.translation: 天气很糟糕，尽管如此，我们还是出去了。

vocabulary.entry: futurist [n.] /ˈfjuːtʃərɪst/ 未来学家
vocabulary.example: Futurists predict major changes in the next decade.
vocabulary.translation: 未来学家预测未来十年将有重大变化。

vocabulary.entry: compress [v.] /kəmˈpres/ 压缩；精简
vocabulary.example: The course compresses two years of study into six months.
vocabulary.translation: 这门课程将两年的学习压缩到六个月。

vocabulary.entry: idiosyncrasy [n.] /ˌɪdiəˈsɪŋkrəsi/ 特质；习性
vocabulary.example: Her idiosyncrasies make her unique.
vocabulary.translation: 她的特质使她与众不同。

vocabulary.entry: reference point [n.] /ˈrefərəns pɔɪnt/ 参照点；参考标准

vocabulary.translation: 以去年的销售额作为参照点。

vocabulary.translation: 科学家们正试图破解这种疾病的密码。

vocabulary.entry: embrace [v.] /ɪmˈbreɪs/ 接受；拥抱 (书面语)

vocabulary.translation: 我们应该接受新技术。

vocabulary.example: Artificial intelligence is changing the world.
vocabulary.translation: 人工智能正在改变世界。

vocabulary.translation: 这家慈善机构致力于社会公益事业。

vocabulary.entry: face-to-face [adj.] /ˌfeɪs tə ˈfeɪs/ 面对面的
vocabulary.example: Face-to-face communication is more effective.
vocabulary.translation: 面对面的交流更有效。

vocabulary.entry: stimulation [n.] /ˌstɪmjʊˈleɪʃən/ 激励；刺激
